subject: Urgent: Q2 commit triage — stage reclass, PO timing & contingency micro-plan
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Q2 commit triage: DataForge stage drift + PO timing

Team — quick heads up on DataForge (DF-2027-ACV-72K). They verbally committed to start in May but procurement just surfaced a multi-week PO approval (finance + legal) that pushes potential payment to mid-June. Today’s check shows their deal has moved from "Commit" to a soft "At Risk" due to PO timing.

Summary: 
- ACV: $72k annual
- Current stage: Contract 
- Risk: Procurement lead time (PO + internal SOW review) likely >30 days
- External ask: DF needs our sample SOW updated + a PO template they can fill immediately (they prefer a single vendor PO).

Immediate asks: 
1) Sales owner (Marissa) — confirm if customer will accept a short pilot invoice or needs vendor-style PO only. Can you confirm pros/cons by EOD?
2) Finance (Mateo) — can Redwood issue a 30-day invoice/bridge or a proforma to keep the revenue in Q2 while PO clears? If not, what is the quickest alternative?
3) Naomi — I want a one-line R/Y/G classification after replies; we'll include this in the commit snapshot.

Attachments: I attached the DF-PO-template.pdf they sent (redacted) and their annotated redlines.

Plan I propose (micro-plan): 
- If finance can provide a 30-day invoice/bridge, we keep as COMMIT -> green with contingency. 
- If not, shift to YELLOW and prepare a reduced-scope pilot (30% of ACV) to start in May to preserve ARR motion.

Please reply with owners/action items. Ill escalate to Jason if we get a hard "no" from finance.

Thanks — Soojin
--
Soojin Lee
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q2 commit triage: DataForge stage drift + PO timing

Thanks Soojin — quick read: 
- Customer position (I spoke with Caroline this morning): they prefer the PO route because procurement needs a vendor PO number to reconcile budgets. Contract redlines are minor (two liability clauses).
- Pilot: Caroline said a pilot is possible, but theyd prefer to avoid splitting the scope because it complicates budget approvals.

Recommendation: 
- Short-term: pursue finance bridge invoice (preferred) — keeps deal green.
- Parallel: circulate the edited SOW + DF-PO-template back to Caroline with our suggested language; ask procurement to start their approval loop while finance issues the bridge.

Action: I will send updated SOW to Caroline by 2pm PT and request confirmation procurement has started the PO workflow. If Caroline confirms procurement started by EOD, mark RYG -> YELLOW to reflect risk but active mitigation.

Marissa
--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 13:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q2 commit triage: DataForge stage drift + PO timing

Marissa / Soojin — thanks for the heads up and the draft. A couple of clarifications from procurement: 
- Our PO approvals run through three approvers (manager, budget owner, central procurement). With our schedule next week, earliest PO signing is likely the week of June 7.
- We cannot pay a proforma invoice unless the vendor is already in our vendor registry (we are processing Redwood but that can take 7–10 business days).
- We are willing to accept a short-term "engagement letter" + 30-day pilot invoice to start internal testing, but procurement says they need a vendor PO number to move forward on full contract payment.

Attached: annotated redlines (DF-contract-redlines-annotated.docx). I will confirm by 5pm PT if procurement can initiate the vendor registry on Monday.

Caroline
Procurement Lead | DataForge
caroline.wu@dataforge.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Q2 commit triage: DataForge stage drift + PO timing

Thanks Caroline and Marissa — useful clarity. Mateo, tagging you: based on procurements timeline, we risk missing our Q2 recognition if we wait for PO. Two options to rescue the commit: 

Option A (preferred): Redwood issues a 30-day "bridge" invoice tied to an engagement letter (low risk for us) so the customer can start in May; procurement completes vendor registry and full PO for subsequent invoices.

Option B (fallback): Convert to a reduced-scope pilot (30% ACV) with immediate start; remainder invoiced after PO clears. This lowers initial ARR but may preserve momentum.

Please advise: can finance issue a bridge invoice (Option A) and which accounting/legal approvals would be required? If theres a standard finance template we can attach to the engagement letter, include it.

Im marking this thread RYG=YELLOW for the commit snapshot until we get confirmation from finance/procurement.

— Soojin

Folks — finance can support a one-time bridge invoice under the following constraints: 
1) Legal needs a short engagement letter (one page) that explicitly states the 30-day payment term and scope. Legal will sign off on the engagement letter; Ill loop in contracts if needed but this should be standard.
2) We will treat the bridge invoice as a short-term AR item; accounting will reclass when PO hits. No revenue recognition until the service start is confirmed per ASC rules — operations should confirm go-live date.
3) I can prepare a "finance bridge invoice" template (finance-bridge-invoice-template.xlsx) and push for an expedited approval. Need the SOW/engagement letter by EOD Monday to move the paperwork.

Next steps / action owners: 
- Marissa: share final SOW/engagement letter with legal + Caroline by 2pm PT Monday.
- Soojin: prepare the engagement letter draft using the attached template and set reminder for legal review.
- Naomi: after Caroline confirms procurement start, update RYG in the commit snapshot.

If we get the engagement letter and customer sign-off, finance will issue the bridge invoice within 48 hours. That should keep the deal in the commit rollout for Q2 reporting purposes (subject to revenue recognition rules).

Ill start the template and upload the DocuSign link once legal confirms.

Thanks — Mateo
